newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes tiptoe higher, Brent uncertain.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes tiptoe higher, Brent uncertain.

text.p: North Sea crudes edged cautiously higher on Friday as refineries took advantage of weak differentials and a paper market contango to snap up a handful of cargoes loading in late April, traders said.
"It's beginning to pick up, partly because storage is working for some and because margins are healthy," said one.
Oseberg loading April 17-19 traded at Dated Brent less 20 cents a barrel, 10 cents firmer than Thursday's deal for an April 16-18 stem.
UK Forties was also looking stronger, helped by contango buying and the cancellation of a chunk of the April programme.

Six Forties cargoes, due to load in the second and third decades of the month, have been cancelled because of lower than expected production at one of the fields feeding Britain's biggest crude stream.
Forties loading April 21-23 and April 24-26 fetched Dated Brent -7 and -5 cents respectively, up to 10 cents firmer than recent deals for cargoes loading a couple of days earlier.
Traders said some buyers were staying clear of Brent and picking up other crudes instead amid continued uncertainty about the fate of at least six second decade cargoes in the hands of Shell.
Shell was considering arbitrage options but given the relatively narrow WTI-Brent spread could be forced to resell the cargoes back into Europe, traders said.
May Brent gained six cents to $18.24 a barrel by 1517 GMT, but intermonth spreads were unmoved and next week's Contracts for Difference slipped a couple of cents to talk at June Brent -$1.02/-$0.92.
Two Brents were expected to be nominated loading dates of April 20-22 and April 21-23 on Friday.
